target: Mae e'n ddoethach nawr.
english: He's wiser now.
tip: Add -ach to an adjective for the comparative. doeth (wise) becomes ddoethach here, wiser.

target: Mae e'n gogydd proffesiynol.
english: He's a professional cook.
tip: yn before a noun softens its first letter. cogydd (cook) becomes gogydd in mae e'n gogydd.

target: Oes angen help arnoch chi?
english: Do you need help?
tip: Need uses angen with ar. Oes angen help arnoch chi means do you need help, help on you.

target: Dw i'n hoffi wyau yn fawr.
english: I like eggs very much.
tip: yn fawr after hoffi means a lot. hoffi wyau yn fawr means like eggs very much.

target: Mae'n gymylog ac oer.
english: It is cloudy and cold.
tip: Welsh starts with the verb. Mae'n gymylog means it is cloudy, the verb Mae coming first.

target: Oes tocynnau ar ôl?
english: Are there any tickets left?
tip: ar ôl here means left or remaining. Oes tocynnau ar ôl means are there tickets left.

target: Noswaith dda, sut mae pethau?
english: Good evening, how are things?
tip: A feminine noun softens its adjective. noswaith is feminine, so da becomes dda in Noswaith dda.

target: Beth ydy'ch rhif ffôn chi?
english: What is your phone number?
tip: Your wraps the noun: eich or 'ch before, chi after. ydy'ch rhif ffôn chi means your phone number.

target: Dw i'n falch o fy nghanlyniadau.
english: I'm proud of my results.
tip: Adjectives take o for of. falch o means proud of, as in falch o fy nghanlyniadau.

target: Mae hi'n dal y trên cynnar.
english: She catches the early train.
tip: yn before a verb-noun marks an ongoing action. mae hi'n dal y trên means she catches the train.

target: Dw i'n dod o Gaerdydd yn wreiddiol.
english: I come from Cardiff originally.
tip: o (from) triggers soft mutation. Caerdydd becomes Gaerdydd in dod o Gaerdydd.

target: Beth ydy'ch enw chi, os gwelwch yn dda?
english: What is your name, please?
tip: os gwelwch yn dda means please, literally if you see well. It ends a polite request.

target: Bore da, sut dych chi heddiw?
english: Good morning, how are you today?
tip: Adjectives follow the noun in Welsh. Bore da is literally morning good, meaning good morning.

target: Sut dych chi? Dw i'n dda, diolch.
english: How are you? I'm fine, thanks.
tip: yn softens an adjective. da becomes dda after yn, as in Dw i'n dda, I am fine.

target: Mae hi'n gwirfoddoli yn y banc bwyd.
english: She volunteers at the food bank.
tip: yn also means in for places. yn y banc bwyd means in the food bank, unlike the linking 'n.

target: Rydyn ni'n bwyta cinio am un o'r gloch.
english: We eat lunch at one o'clock.
tip: o'r gloch means o'clock, literally of the bell. am un o'r gloch means at one o'clock.

target: Oes gyda chi frawd neu chwaer?
english: Do you have a brother or sister?
tip: In south Wales possession uses gyda. Oes gyda chi frawd means do you have a brother.

target: Dych chi'n gwybod ble mae'r amgueddfa?
english: Do you know where the museum is?
tip: An embedded question keeps normal order. ble mae'r amgueddfa means where the museum is.

target: Noswaith dda, ydych chi eisiau diod?
english: Good evening, would you like a drink?
tip: eisiau, to want, takes no yn before it. ydych chi eisiau diod means do you want a drink.

target: Oes bwyty da yn y dref?
english: Is there a good restaurant in town?
tip: Feminine nouns soften after y. tref (town) becomes dref in yn y dref.

target: Faint o fyfyrwyr sydd yn y dosbarth?
english: How many students are in the class?
tip: Faint o means how many before a noun. Faint o fyfyrwyr means how many students.

target: Caodd hi'r siop am chwech o'r gloch.
english: She closed the shop at six o'clock.
tip: The ending -odd marks past for he or she. Caodd hi means she closed.

target: Dyw e ddim yn gwybod ble mae'r allweddi.
english: He doesn't know where the keys are.
tip: Negatives add ddim. Dyw e ddim yn gwybod means he does not know, Dyw being negative mae.

target: Mae ganddo fo bedwar brawd a dwy chwaer.
english: He has four brothers and two sisters.
tip: Two has genders: dau for masculine, dwy for feminine. chwaer is feminine, so dwy chwaer.

target: Bydd y siop yn cau am chwech o'r gloch.
english: The shop will close at six o'clock.
tip: Bydd is the future of bod for 'he/she/it'. Add yn before the verb: Bydd y siop yn cau (the shop will close).

target: Mae angen dau docyn arnon ni ar gyfer y sioe.
english: We need two tickets for the show.
tip: The number dau softens the next noun. tocyn becomes docyn in dau docyn, two tickets.

target: Mae e mor dal â'i dad erbyn hyn.
english: He is as tall as his father now.
tip: mor plus â means as ... as. mor dal â'i dad means as tall as his father.

target: Oes bara neu gaws ar ôl gyda ti?
english: Do you have any bread or cheese left?
tip: neu (or) triggers soft mutation. caws (cheese) becomes gaws in bara neu gaws.

target: Mae e'n canu'n uwch na phawb yn y côr.
english: He sings louder than everyone in the choir.
tip: na (than) triggers aspirate mutation on p, t, c. pawb becomes phawb in na phawb.

target: Oes signal ffôn da yma yn y pentref?
english: Is there good phone signal here in the village?
tip: oes asks if something exists, ydy asks about a known thing. Oes signal ffôn da yma means is there phone signal here.
